title: Grocery Supply Chain KPIs: Why Compliance Predicts the Rest
summary: Grocery supply chain KPIs start with compliance. Learn the five metrics grocery and CPG suppliers should track, from OTIF to chargeback rate, and why.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


Why grocery suppliers face strict delivery standards on the weakest data foundation of any segment


-


How compliance rate, fill rate, and chargeback rate connect to one another


-


What realistic inventory turnover looks like for food and beverage brands


Grocery supply chain KPIs usually start with fill rate and on-time delivery, because retailers measure those first. A guide for consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands selling to Kroger says suppliers must maintain at least 98% on-time delivery and a 95% fill rate to avoid penalties. However, according to[SPS Commerce network data spanning six industries](https://us-east-1.graphassets.com/AaZQD68KNQ46abk6wQUdWz/cmqfk5xqu3fhy07iu48n2u5do) , the grocery sector had the lowest trading partner compliance rate: 31.6% against a 42.8% cross-industry average.


Compliance sits underneath the delivery numbers. It describes how accurately trading partners exchange the documents that run a supply chain through[electronic data interchange (EDI)](https://www.spscommerce.com/what-is-edi/) . When compliance is weak, fill rate and on-time performance suffer, causing deductions to pile up.


## What Delivery Standards Do Grocery Suppliers Face?


Retailers set clear targets and attach penalties to them. For example, Walmart requires 98%[On Time In Full (OTIF)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/why-is-otif-important) compliance and charges 3% of the cost of goods sold for noncompliance.


Each retailer also calculates these measures in its own way. A supplier selling to several grocery chains therefore tracks several versions of the same metric. Retailers also regularly revise their thresholds, so the current vendor guide is the final word on any single number.


## What Does EDI Compliance Rate by Industry Show?


SPS defines trading partner compliance as the simple average of three participation rates:[order confirmations (EDI 855)](https://www.spscommerce.com/edi-document/edi-855-purchase-order-acknowledgment/) ,[advance ship notices (ASN, EDI 856),](https://www.spscommerce.com/edi-document/edi-856-advance-shipping-notice/) and[invoices (EDI 810)](https://www.spscommerce.com/edi-document/edi-810-electronic-invoice/) . A supplier that sends all three on time counts as compliant. The data covers more than 4,000 buying organizations, so it shows how well suppliers participate when they sell to each segment.

At 31.6%, fewer than one in three supplier interactions in grocery produces reliable inputs for forecasting and replenishment. Each document feeds a different process: receiving, allocation, or payment. A gap in any of them later shows up as a short shipment, a late arrival, or a delayed payment.


SPS attributes the gap to structure. Suppliers on structured networks reach 81.6% blended compliance, compared with 45.5% in proprietary systems, and the same suppliers perform very differently for different buyers. Unclear vendor guides, outdated contact records, and no closed loop showing that a requirement change arrived all contribute.


## What Does the OTIF Benchmark Grocery Retailers Set Look Like?


OTIF measures whether a shipment arrives on schedule with the full ordered quantity. Fill rate covers the quantity side alone, as the share of ordered cases a supplier ships. Grocery benchmarks come from each retailer’s program.


Eagle Foods makes canned condensed milk and snack foods. Its team used centralized reporting and carrier scorecards to trace Walmart deductions back to carrier and warehouse performance. That visibility helped raise its[average monthly prepaid On Time score by 16.7%](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/eagle-foods-case-study/) .


**Related Reading:**[How to Improve Your OTIF Performance](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/improving-otif-performance)


## What Is a Realistic CPG Inventory Turnover Benchmark?


Inventory turnover is the cost of goods sold divided by the average inventory. For grocery, convenience and fast-moving consumer goods, there are roughly 12 to 20 or more turns a year overall. Individual brands tend to report lower figures. An analysis of FY2025 annual filings found that[public beverage brands turn inventory between 3.9 and 9.5 times a year](https://eightx.co/blog/beverage-brand-inventory-planning) , with a median near 4.8. The same firm’s review of food brands found[turns of roughly 4.5 to 20 a year](https://eightx.co/blog/food-brand-inventory-planning) , depending on shelf life.


No single number applies across the category. A brand’s own history, plus peers with similar shelf life and channel mix, make a better comparison than a category average.


## What Is a Typical Grocery Supplier Chargeback Rate?


The gross chargeback rate is the total deduction dollars divided by the gross revenue, multiplied by 100. The net chargeback rate divides net deduction dollars by net revenue. It adjusts for returns, allowances, and money won back through disputes. According to SPS, suppliers can[lose an estimated 5% to 7% of retail revenue](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/revenue-recovery-metrics) to erroneous charges. The same article sets no universal target. It suggests that each supplier should build a baseline by retailer, product category, and fulfillment model.


Two food suppliers show what disputing can recover.[Eagle Foods](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/eagle-foods-case-study/) disputed $421,500 in invalid Walmart deductions over seven months and reached a 92% win rate.[Chosen Foods](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/chosen-foods-case-study/) identified $1.1 million in deductions across retailers and distributors, including Kroger, KeHE, and UNFI. It recovered $367,000 in its first year.


**Related Reading:**[EDI Chargebacks Explained](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-chargebacks-explained)


## How Does Working Capital Tie the Metrics Together?


The metrics connect in sequence:


1.


A supplier sends a late, incomplete, or inaccurate ship notice.


1.


The receiving dock can’t match the shipment to the order, so the grocer logs a shortage or late arrival.


1.


The miss counts against the supplier’s fill rate or on-time score and triggers a deduction.


1.


The deduction reduces the remittance, and the dispute holds the cash until it resolves.


An[SPS analysis of more than $9.7 billion in grocery order volume](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/margin-pressure-in-grocery-the-hidden-working-capital-tax) found $634 million caught in volatile transactions. These are unresolved exceptions, compliance failures, and execution gaps. The same article reports that rework can consume up to 9% of a product’s cost of goods sold. SPS estimates that a 1% reduction in transaction volatility frees $9–10 million in cash flow. The analysis measures costs on the grocer’s side, which helps explain why retailers attach fines to compliance misses.


## How Often Should Grocery Suppliers Review Each Metric?


Fill rate and OTIF change with every shipment, so a weekly review catches problems while the evidence is fresh. The other metrics move more slowly or depend on reconciliation cycles, so a monthly or quarterly review fits better.

## Want To See Every Trading Partner in One View?


Tracking these numbers retailer by retailer means rebuilding each one from separate portals and reports.[SPS Commerce Decision Intelligence](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/analytics/) gives suppliers standardized visibility across trading partners. Compliance, fill rate, and chargeback figures then come from one consistent source.


Not ready for new tooling?[The Supply Chain Source](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/) has articles and vendor guides for suppliers selling into grocery and retail.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What are the most important grocery supply chain KPIs for suppliers?


The five metrics covered here are compliance rate, OTIF and fill rate, inventory turnover, chargeback rate, and working capital. Compliance rate sits underneath the others because it measures the documents that drive receiving, allocation, and payment.


### What is trading partner compliance in grocery?


It is the simple average of how accurately suppliers send order confirmations, advance ship notices, and invoices. SPS network data puts the grocery average at 31.6%, the lowest of the segments studied.


### What is the difference between gross and net chargeback rate?


Gross chargeback rate measures deductions against gross revenue. Net chargeback rate measures deductions against net revenue after returns, allowances, and recovered revenue. It shows the financial impact that remains after successful disputes.


*Benchmarks in this article are directional ranges drawn from the sources cited, and they do not promise any specific result. Retailer requirements change, so suppliers should double-check current thresholds in each retailer’s vendor guide.*
